quote: Herein we show an enhancement of the room-temperature lithium-ion conductivity by 3 orders of magnitude through the creation of nanostructured Li(3)PS(4).
explanation: I got the abstract from both OpenAlex and the PubMed record (PMID 23305294) in Valency. It gives no absolute conductivity values, so I cannot confirm 1.6e-4 S/cm or 2.6e-7 S/cm from the text I retrieved. Following the task rule, the verdict is UNCLEAR. The evidence leans clearly toward a physical difference rather than a database error, though. The abstract compares two different materials. One is nanoporous beta-Li3PS4, the high-conduction phase stabilised by the nanostructure. The other is bulk Li3PS4, which at room temperature is the poorly conducting gamma phase. The abstract says the room-temperature conductivity goes up "by 3 orders of magnitude" from one to the other. The flagged gap is log10(1.6e-4 / 2.6e-7) = 2.79, a factor of about 615, which matches that 3-order claim. So the two databases most likely took different samples from the same paper: Liverpool the nanoporous beta value, OBELiX the bulk value (or the other way round). Each record is probably a correct transcription of its own sample. The unit-error idea (mS/cm stored as S/cm) is off by 0.21 dex, and nothing in the source supports it. The two-polymorph explanation fits the gap without it. If the full text confirms both numbers (about 1.6e-4 S/cm for nanoporous beta and about 3e-7 S/cm for bulk gamma at 25 C), this becomes physical_difference (different sample/polymorph in the same paper). The fix would then be to label the sample or phase in both databases, not to correct either value.
